class.name: NetwLinkConditions
class.brief_description: Author-time latency and loss simulation for a session's own outbound peer.
class.description: Delays are authored in milliseconds and loss as a percent, the units a game designer tunes in, and [method wrap_peer] is what converts them: [member one_way_delay_min] and [member one_way_delay_max] scale down to seconds and [member lag_packet_loss_percent] scales down to a ratio, which are the units [code]LaggyMultiplayerPeer[/code] takes. Install one through [member NetwSessionConfig.link_conditions], authored beside the transport it tunes, and [NetwMultiplayer] wraps the built peer with it at bring-up. [codeblock] var conditions := NetwLinkConditions.new() conditions.simulate_lag = true conditions.one_way_delay_max = 150.0 conditions.lag_packet_loss_percent = 2.0 config.link_conditions = conditions [/codeblock] [method wrap_peer] returns the peer it was given unchanged, with a warning, when [member simulate_lag] is on but the build carries no [code]LaggyMultiplayerPeer[/code] extension. A missing simulator is a reason to run without it, never a reason the session fails to come up. This is a development tool. [method wrap_peer] returns the original peer in release exports, regardless of [member simulate_lag]. Compare the returned peer with the input to determine whether simulation is active. A debug build and the editor shape their link, and a release export does not. [code]NETW_SHAPING[/code] in the environment, or [code]--netw-shaping=on|off[/code] on the command line, overrides that in both directions, for the playtest shipped on a debug template and for the release build a tester needs to impair. The environment wins over the flag, and a value that is neither an on word ([code]on[/code], [code]1[/code], [code]true[/code], [code]yes[/code]) nor an off word ([code]off[/code], [code]0[/code], [code]false[/code], [code]no[/code]) is no override at all, so a typo cannot quietly impair a shipped build. The impairment applies to this session's own peer, so it shapes every link that peer carries at once. A server wrapped this way is slow to every client rather than to one, and per-remote-peer impairment exists only on the loopback, through [method LocalLoopbackSession.set_link_conditions].

method.name: wrap_peer
method.description: Returns [param base] wrapped in a [code]LaggyMultiplayerPeer[/code] carrying this spec's delays and loss, converted to the wrapper's units. Returns [param base] itself when [member simulate_lag] is [code]false[/code], when [param base] is [code]null[/code], when this build does not shape its link, or when the wrapper class is unavailable or publishes no [code]create[/code]. [b]Note:[/b] Impairment also needs the optional [code]LaggyMultiplayerPeer[/code] extension present in the build. A build that shapes its link but carries no simulator still returns [param base].

members.member: Percent chance a packet is dropped, clamped to [code]0..100[/code] by [method wrap_peer]. Authored as a percent and converted to a ratio for the wrapper.
The upper bound of the simulated one-way delay, in milliseconds. [method wrap_peer] floors it at [member one_way_delay_min].
The lower bound of the simulated one-way delay, in milliseconds. [method wrap_peer] floors it at zero.
Whether [method wrap_peer] wraps the peer at all. [code]false[/code] returns the base peer untouched, so a spec left on a config with this off costs nothing.
